To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) The memory hierarchy depth of a system is the most critical factor affecting the execution times for many workloads; 2) The memory hierarchy depths of different workloads are different, and 3) The memory hierarchy of an SMP is more expensive than that of a cluster.

the depth of memory hierarchy has the largest impact on the performance of a cluster, and that a cluster with a deeper memory hierarchy is more cost-effective than a cluster of work-stations/PCs with a shallower hierarchy.
the depth of memory hierarch in a cluster is more important than its interconnect network, and that the depth of a tightly-coupled memory hierachy is more important than the number of processors.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following three issues: (1) to build an analytical model for cluster computing, (2) to use the model to study the performance impact of different memory hierarchy configurations on cluster computing, and (3) to provide quantitative recommendations on building cost-effective clusters.
the following questions: How does a memory hierarchy affect the performance of cluster computing? Which memory hierarchy configuration is most cost-effective for a certain workload?

the following questions: How to evaluate the performance impact of the memory hierarchy of an SMP, a cluster, and an SMP cluster? How to evaluate the impact of the interconnection network on the cluster performance? How to build cost-effective clusters?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a cluster of PCs with a memory depth of 4 or more is the most cost-effective platform for most workloads.
the memory hierarchy depth is the most critical parameter in determining the performance of cluster computing.
for a cluster of work-stations/PCs, the cost of the interconnection network is the most sensitive parameter for the execution time of many workloads.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cost of a cluster is more sensitive to the depth of its memory hierarchy than its interconnection network.
a cost-effective cluster for parallel computing is not only dependent on the number of processors, but also on the depth of the system memory hierarchy.
a tightly coupled system should not be considered unless it is necessary for a specific workload.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the memory hierarchy is as important as the network for cluster computing.
the memory hierarchy should be carefully designed to meet the needs of the target workloads.
for many types of applications, the memory hierarchy depth is more important than the system cost in determining the performance of a cluster system.
